title: Customer Care Guidance: Battery Replacement Warranties Held by One Customer
content:
**Rule.** A customer may hold any number of Battery Replacement Warranties. Each battery sold opens its own warranty, with its own purchase date, its own core deposit and its own claim history, and warranties never pool free replacements or credits. There is no limit on the number of battery warranties one customer may hold; how many active batteries one vehicle may carry is governed by the per-vehicle limit on active battery warranties.

**What belongs to each warranty, battery by battery**

| Item | Belongs to |
|---|---|
| Purchase date | the warranty of the battery sold on that ticket |
| Core deposit | the warranty of the battery sold on that ticket |
| Claim history (tests, free replacements, prorated adjustments) | the warranty of the battery concerned |
| Free replacements and credits | that warranty alone; never pooled with another warranty |

**Points of judgement**

- *Hypothetical:* a customer holds three Crestline battery warranties on three vehicles. That is three separate warranties, each counted from its own purchase date; the number held by the customer sets no limit.
- *Hypothetical:* a customer has used the free replacement on one battery's warranty and holds a second battery's warranty with no claims on it. The used free replacement belongs to the first warranty only; the second warranty's claim history is its own and is unaffected.
- *Hypothetical:* a prorated credit earned on one battery's warranty is not carried to, or combined with, a credit on another battery's warranty, since warranties never pool credits.
